summary: Curbside pickup MVP targets local businesses in Ashtabula County needing streamlined order-ahead and pickup solutions. Research identified 5 qualified leads across restaurants, food markets, and retail businesses that could benefit from a white-labeled curbside pickup platform.

leads.name: Harbor Gardens
leads.fit_rationale: Active local food market with 50+ vendors, classes, and events. Currently operates a general store but lacks dedicated curbside ordering system. High community engagement and growing local food network makes them ideal for a curbside pickup solution for pre-orders of local produce, prepared foods, and market items.

leads.name: Crosswinds Grille at The Lakehouse Inn
leads.fit_rationale: Already offers limited curbside pickup (Thu-Mon 5:15-7pm) but lacks a dedicated ordering platform. Currently appears to use phone-in orders. A white-labeled curbside solution would streamline their operations and expand their pickup capabilities beyond current limited hours.

leads.name: Ashtabula Farmers Market
leads.fit_rationale: Bridge Street market in Historic Harbor District operating Sundays 10am-2pm. 5,400+ Facebook followers indicates strong community presence. Pre-order curbside pickup would benefit both vendors and customers, especially during peak seasons and festival weekends when parking is limited.

leads.name: 2140 Farm Market
leads.fit_rationale: Located at 2140 State Route 307, Austinburg. Family farm offering fresh produce, home baked goods, and seasonal items. Small rural farm operations like this often lack digital ordering infrastructure but could benefit significantly from curbside pre-ordering to manage harvest inventory and reduce waste.

leads.name: Conneaut Farmers Market
leads.fit_rationale: Operating Saturdays 9am-1pm at Moose Lodge parking lot (280 Park Ave). Serves eastern Ashtabula County area. Curbside pre-ordering would help vendors prepare inventory and serve time-constrained customers who want local produce but can't browse the full market.
leads.source: Ashtabula Local Food Guide + AshtaBeautiful directory

branding_quality_assessment.current_state: The curbside MVP landing page has minimal branding with generic purple gradient styling. No logo, favicon, or visual identity. Typography uses system fonts. Color scheme is basic purple-to-pink gradient without brand cohesion.
branding_quality_assessment.recommended_focus: Position as 'Ashtabula Local Pickup' or similar community-focused brand emphasizing local commerce support. Develop visual identity that resonates with rural/rustic aesthetics while maintaining modern tech appeal.

site_improvements: Add authentic local imagery of Ashtabula County farms and businesses
Include customer testimonials from local business owners
Feature specific use cases: farm stands, restaurants, artisans, service providers
Add trust indicators: 'Proudly serving Ashtabula County since 202X'
Add simple pricing calculator for local business owners

aesthetics_and_layout_notes.current_layout: Clean but generic single-page layout with centered hero section and alternating feature blocks. Responsive design present but uninspired. No local character or regional identity.
improvement_suggestions: Incorporate Lake Erie harbor imagery or rural farm aesthetics
Use earthy, organic color palette (greens, blues, warm neutrals) instead of generic purple
Add 'Ashtabula County Proud' badge or similar regional identifier
Include photo gallery of local businesses that could benefit
Feature map integration showing local service area
Add seasonal theming (fall harvest, spring market, etc.)

whitelabel_potential.rationale: High potential for whitelabel deployment. The curbside pickup concept is universal but implementation needs local branding. Can be customized per business type: farm stands (rustic), restaurants (modern), retail (professional). API-first architecture would enable integration with existing local business websites.
target_customizations: Harbor Gardens: Rustic/artisan food market theme
Crosswinds Grille: Upscale farm-to-table restaurant theme

action_next: Contact Harbor Gardens first as they represent the strongest fit with established community presence, physical location, and demonstrated need for order management. Follow up with Crosswinds Grille who already understand curbside value but need better technology. Approach farmers markets as group pilot opportunity.

notes: Research conducted March 22, 2026. Ashtabula County shows strong local food movement with established farmers markets and farm stands. Most businesses rely on phone orders or third-party delivery apps (DoorDash, UberEats) which charge high commissions. A local-focused, low-cost curbside pickup solution would fill a clear market gap. The county's rural nature (limited transportation, spread-out population) makes curbside pickup particularly valuable for accessibility.
